intro.title: Start Here
intro.lede: A short orientation for teachers new to Wewoka High — what a walk-through looks for, what belongs on your board, how to unpack a standard, and how the curriculum and your resources relate. Watch each short video and skim the notes.

principalLookFors.title: What your principal is looking for
principalLookFors.description: A quick, honest picture of what walk-throughs are checking — bell-to-bell instruction, a posted objective, cognitive work by students, and feedback tied to a criterion.
lookFors: Bell-to-bell instruction (start on time, end on task)
Students doing the cognitive work — talking, writing, solving
Feedback tied to a criterion, not just praise

board.title: What to put on the board
board.description: A simple board setup that supports a walk-through in five seconds: standard, objective in student-friendly language, agenda, and success criteria.

video.title: I CAN Statements as Classroom Objectives

items: Success criteria — how a student knows they’ve got it

unpack.title: Breaking down a state standard
unpack.description: Turn a dense standard into the specific skills and knowledge students will need. This is the planning move that saves you every other planning step.

video.title: An Overview of Unpacking the Standards

steps: Identify the nouns (what students must know)
Identify the verbs (what students must do)
Decide the level of thinking (recall, apply, analyze, create)
Write the “I can…” statement students will see

curriculumVsResources.title: Curriculum vs. resources
curriculumVsResources.description: Your curriculum is the plan; your textbook and worksheets are tools. Don’t confuse the two — the standard drives the plan, and your resources serve the standard.

video.title: Practice Teaching — Books are Resources, not Curriculum

compare.label: Curriculum
compare.detail: The state standards + your plan to teach them, in order.

compare.label: Resources
compare.detail: Textbook, worksheets, videos, sites — chosen to serve the standard.

onYourFeet.title: On your feet and moving
onYourFeet.description: The single highest-leverage classroom management move at the secondary level. Circulate, scan, and interact — proximity does most of the work.

video.title: Proximity Control — High School Example & Non-Example

techniques: Proximity control — stand near where behavior is drifting
Active supervision — move, scan, interact every few minutes
Strategic circulation — plan your route around the room

items.name: HELPS — Helping Early Literacy with Practice Strategies
items.subject: Reading fluency
items.description: A structured fluency routine: adult models a passage, student does repeated readings, errors get phrase-drill correction, then a retell check and reward. Well-studied for struggling readers.

resources.title: IES Practice Guide — Improving Adolescent Literacy

items.citation: Begeny, J. C., Ross, S. G., Greene, D. J., Mitchell, R. C., & Whitehouse, M. H. (2012).

items.name: Group-Based Repeated Reading
items.subject: Reading fluency
items.format: ~15 min; groups of up to 3; 2–3 times per week
items.description: A short, high-dosage fluency routine for a small group: passage preview, three repeated readings, phrase-drill error correction, and a contingent reward. Works when passages are at each student’s instructional level (~90% accuracy).

items.name: Corrective Reading (SRA / McGraw-Hill)
items.subject: Decoding & comprehension
items.format: Small group; teacher-directed; 2–3 times per week
items.description: A published program with placement tests and scripted lessons across decoding and comprehension strands. Pace and grouping are set from a placement test so students work at their true instructional level.

video.title: Corrective Reading Program — Decoding Training Overview

resources.title: IES Practice Guide — Improving Adolescent Literacy

items.name: Reciprocal Teaching
items.subject: Reading comprehension
items.format: Small group; each student rotates through four roles
items.description: Students take turns leading a discussion using the four moves — predict, question, clarify, summarize — while working through a shared text. Builds active comprehension habits that transfer to independent reading.

resources.title: IES Practice Guide — Improving Adolescent Literacy

items.name: Question-Answer Relationships (QAR)
items.subject: Reading comprehension
items.format: Small group or whole class; can be paired with any text
items.description: Teaches students to recognize four question types (Right There, Think & Search, Author & Me, On My Own) and where the answer lives. Immediately improves how students attack test questions and reading tasks.

resources.title: IES Practice Guide — Improving Adolescent Literacy

items.name: Concrete–Representational–Abstract (CRA)
items.subject: Math conceptual understanding
items.format: Small group or 1:1; multiple sessions per concept
items.description: Teach a new concept first with a physical object (concrete), then with a drawing or picture (representational), then with numbers and symbols (abstract). The bridge from physical to symbolic is where struggling learners break down — CRA rebuilds it.

resources.title: IRIS Center — High-Quality Math Instruction (CRA page)
IES Practice Guide — Assisting Students Struggling with Mathematics

items.name: Cognitive Strategy Instruction for Math
items.subject: Math problem solving
items.format: Small group or 1:1; explicit modeling → guided → independent
items.description: Give students a named, step-by-step strategy for attacking word problems — teacher models it aloud (think-aloud), students practice with feedback, then release. WWC-reviewed.

video.title: HLP #14 — Use Cognitive and Metacognitive Strategies

resources.title: IES Practice Guide — Improving Mathematical Problem Solving (Grades 4–8)

items.name: PALS for Math (Peer-Assisted Learning Strategies)
items.subject: Math computation & problem solving
items.format: Pairs (higher–lower); ~30 min sessions; multiple times per week
items.description: Structured peer tutoring. Students alternate the Coach and Player roles working through a set problem sequence. Everyone gets more practice repetitions than a teacher-led lesson can provide alone.

items.name: Schema-Based Instruction (word problems)
items.subject: Math word-problem solving
items.format: Small group; concept-based sequence (Total, Difference, Change, Ratio)
items.description: Teaches students to identify the underlying schema of a word problem (combining amounts, comparing, changing over time) and match it to a solution structure — not just hunt for keywords.

video.title: Additive Schemas — Total Schema, Word Problems (Project STAIR)

resources.title: IES Practice Guide — Improving Mathematical Problem Solving (Grades 4–8)

items.name: Explicit Timed Fact / Math Fluency Intervention
items.subject: Math fact fluency
items.format: Small group or 1:1; short daily timings + progress chart
items.description: Direct, explicit practice of a small set of facts with 1-minute timings, immediate feedback, and a visible progress chart. Best used in short blocks alongside conceptual instruction, not as a substitute for it.

video.title: HLP #14 — Use Cognitive and Metacognitive Strategies (background)

resources.title: National Center on Intensive Intervention — Academic Interventions

items.name: Self-Regulated Strategy Development (SRSD)
items.subject: Writing (with reading transfer)
items.format: Small group; six-stage sequence with mnemonics like POW + TREE
items.description: A structured approach that teaches students both a writing strategy (e.g., POW for planning; TREE for persuasive essays) and self-regulation habits (goal setting, self-monitoring). One of the most-studied writing interventions.

video.title: SRSD in Action — A Reading/Writing Case Study (Dr. Karen Harris)
video.channel: SRSD Online: The Science of Writing

items.name: PALS for Writing (Argumentative)
items.subject: Argumentative writing
items.format: Pairs; Coach and Writer roles; multi-session unit
items.description: Peer-tutoring version of PALS applied to argumentative writing. Students plan, draft, revise, and edit in pairs using a shared strategy. Effective for adolescents.

items.name: Check-In / Check-Out — Academic version
items.subject: Work completion, organization, engagement
items.format: Brief daily; mentor check-in AM + check-out PM; teacher point sheet
items.description: Student picks up a daily point sheet from a mentor before school. Teachers rate agreed-upon behaviors each period (in class, on task, work turned in). Student checks out at the end of the day. Fast to set up, high dosage, works well for the “on the bubble” students.

resources.title: PBIS.org — Check-in Check-out: A Targeted Intervention
